Values at many points from a SpatProxy

Source: R/proxy_extract.R
extract-SpatProxy.Rd

extract() reads the value of a gridded variable at each point of a SpatVector3D, for many points at once. It gives the same values as calling mask(as_voxel(crop(proxy, p), time = p), p) for each point p, much faster: the points are matched to time steps together, and each time step is read once, cropped to its points. The article vignette("workflow-values-in-shapes") shows it in "Many points at once".

Usage

# S4 method for class 'SpatProxy,SpatVector3D'
extract(
  x,
  y,
  method = c("nearest", "nearest_level", "bottom", "surface"),
  time_match = c("nearest", "exact"),
  max_time_diff = NULL,
  bind = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A SpatProxy, from as_proxy(): a netCDF file, a series of files, or a voxel in memory.

y

SpatVector3D points, from as_vector3d().

method

For a variable with depth, the depth level each point takes: "nearest" (default), "nearest_level", "bottom" or "surface", as in mask(). method sets the depth level; time_match sets the time step.

time_match, max_time_diff

How a point's time is matched to a time step, as in as_voxel(): "nearest" (default), the step nearest in time, or "exact"; and for nearest matching, the largest gap in days. NULL (default) sets no limit. These set the time step; method sets the depth level.

bind

FALSE (default) for a data frame of the values; TRUE for the points themselves with the values added, as terra's extract(raster, vector, bind = TRUE) returns the vector.

...

Not used.

Value

With bind = FALSE, a data frame with one row per point, in the order of y:

  • feature_id, the point's ID;

  • value, NA for a point off the grid, without a matching time step, or with no level its method can take;

  • time_step, the date-time of the time step used, NA for a source without dated steps or a point with no matching step. A point off the grid keeps its step's time;

  • depth_level, the depth of the level used in metres, NA for a variable without depth or when value is NA.

With bind = TRUE, y itself, a SpatVector3D with the same features in the same order and all their columns, plus value, time_step and depth_level as above. They aren't named time and depth in either form, because a point already has its own time and depth. Points with a column named value, time_step or depth_level stop with an error; rename the column first.

Details

Each point takes the time step nearest its time, or the step equal to it with time_match = "exact", as as_voxel() matches a point. With dates, a point's date matches by UTC day. A climatology with one time step, such as a World Ocean Atlas annual field, gives that step to every point, whatever its time. On a source with dated time steps, even one, a point without a time gets NA, with a warning.

Each point takes the cell that holds it and, for a variable with depth, one depth level, chosen with method as mask() does for points:

  • "nearest" (default): the level nearest the point's depth, skipping levels without a value, as extract_to_point(method = "nearest") does.

  • "nearest_level": the level nearest the point's depth, even if it has no value.

  • "bottom": the deepest level with a value.

  • "surface": the shallowest level.

For a variable without depth, each point takes the value in its cell, and method doesn't apply.

A time step's points are read together while they are close enough. A group of points is read in smaller groups of nearby points when one read would exceed the read budget (the option ocean3d.max_read_mb, 1024 MB by default), or would hold more than 10,000 cells and depth levels for each point, so that points far apart aren't read with the water between them. The values are the same.

Experimental

SpatProxy and as_proxy() are experimental. Their slots and behaviour may change without notice while the core object is built.

See also

mask() and as_voxel() for one shape at a time; extract_to_point().

Examples

p <- as_proxy(system.file("extdata", "example_3d.nc", package = "ocean3d"))
pts <- as_vector3d(data.frame(
  lon = c(0.1, 0.9), lat = c(40.2, 40.8), depth = c(5, 60),
  date = as.Date(c("2020-01-01", "2020-01-05"))
), time = "date")
terra::extract(p, pts)
#>   feature_id value  time_step depth_level
#> 1          1    20 2020-01-01           0
#> 2          2    19 2020-01-06          50

# The deepest level with a value at each point instead.
terra::extract(p, pts, method = "bottom")
#>   feature_id value  time_step depth_level
#> 1          1    10 2020-01-01         100
#> 2          2    14 2020-01-06         100

# The points themselves, with the values added to their columns.
as.data.frame(terra::extract(p, pts, bind = TRUE))
#>   feature_id vertex lon  lat depth       time value  time_step depth_level
#> 1          1      1 0.1 40.2     5 2020-01-01    20 2020-01-01           0
#> 2          2      1 0.9 40.8    60 2020-01-05    19 2020-01-06          50
